x: Scratch man was an old friend of many of us, the late George Still. One item reads "members will be pleased to hear that Sgt.J.Cox is on his way home from the front"!
The race ended in a win for W.Berridge off the short mark, for him, of 35yds. G.Still won the 2 miles handicap at Hertford off virtual scratch (65yds) in the fast time of 9:40.6 seconds.

(3rd from right) alongside of whom is the bespectacled Wally Bayliss who was to become our President, but probably retired from this race. Runner up to Footer was Micky Pyer (extreme left) who won in 1923 and 1924; with George Still (extreme right) 3rd.

George Still, who finished third, was the veteran of the field and it seems difficult now to realise that 25 years or so previoulsy, at the turn of the century, he was in winning teams of the Southern Counties and National C.C.

In time he graduated to George Still's training pack where he built up his fitness still further and then set his sights on competitive road racing Arthur has happy memories of those early days in the Club with George, Sid Ring, Bert "Champ" Smith, George Chandler and others, and really enjoyed hims…
His first Saturday afternoon runs were with veteran George Still but he soon graduated to the pack led by the legendary Bert Footer, then in the twilight of his career.
Having won the title in 1923 and 1924, this time he had to give way to his captain Bert Footer. Left to right: A.D.Pyer, A.E.Smith, -, J.G.Flatt, -, -, -, -, H.E.Footer, W.L.Bayliss, G.Still.
Extreme right of the picture was George Still, and Brian fondly remembers his first visit to the Club when George took him out for his initial run over Wimbledon Common.
